name: frontier-allocation-evaluation
status: fixed before any run; no run exists
question: Does coordinated allocation resolve more preregistered, decision-relevant uncertainty than simple policies within the same resource budget?
budget_unit: declared cost unit of the actions' resource_estimate; consumption from a ledger receipt
rules: value per problem is the EVPI under declared utilities, frozen and hashed before any arm runs
an accepted result later overturned by independent review counts as incorrect acceptance and does NOT resolve the problem
a policy is reported as better only if it resolves more problems with exact p < alpha AND is not worse on incorrect acceptance
fewer than min_problems problems: descriptive only, no verdict
budgets that differ by more than the tolerance: comparison refused
premise_note: Models are not assumed inaccurate. An unguarded frontier model scored ~95% on the frozen benchmark; the value measured here is allocation, witness and reuse, not an accuracy gap.
